_about: Hardening PR-7: the walls of docs/design/hardening-pr4-guard-audit.md section 4 (W1-W8), as Claude Code config. A plugin cannot ship permissions or a sandbox, so reef-init merges `settings` into the project's .claude/settings.json (a key the project has is never changed; a rule or host it lacks is added), with sandbox.network.allowedDomains = the hosts below for the detected stack. Defense in depth: the guard keeps every check. Edit rules: `/` is the project root, `~/` home. Sandbox paths: `./` is the project root, `~/` home, `/` the filesystem root.

github.com.why: git fetch/push to the forge over https; cargo audit reads RustSec's advisory db from it

api.github.com.why: gh: the loop's pull requests, checks, merges and the issues queue

registry.npmjs.org.why: npm ci, npx and npm audit (worktree.setup and the release audit gate)

binaries.prisma.sh.why: prisma generate downloads its engines (only when package.json depends on Prisma)

pypi.org.why: pip install -e . / uv sync (the index) and pip-audit (PyPI's vulnerability API)

files.pythonhosted.org.why: the package files pip and uv download

index.crates.io.why: cargo fetch: the sparse crates index

proxy.golang.org.why: go mod download: the module proxy

sum.golang.org.why: go mod download: the checksum database

vuln.go.dev.why: govulncheck: the release audit gate's vulnerability database

semgrep.dev.why: semgrep scan: the injection release gate's rule packs (p/owasp-top-ten and the stack's)
